_nota: Hand-curated data. The keys inside 'cultivos' stay in Spanish because they are the exact SIAP crop names (the pipeline uses them to join with SIAP). 'ecocrop' = scientific name as it appears in the EcoCrop table (if it differs from 'cientifico'). descripcion/suelo/cuidados are a general DRAFT: review them against INIFAP technology packages and fact sheets before publishing them as a recommendation. ciclo_dias here overrides the EcoCrop range, which is usually too wide.

Maíz grano.descripcion: Staple food crop in Mexico and the crop with the largest planted area in the country. It is planted in almost every municipality, both rainfed and irrigated, and has a great diversity of varieties and hybrids adapted to each region.
Maíz grano.suelo: Loamy, deep and well-drained; pH 5.5 to 7.5.
cuidados: Plant into moist soil; under rainfed conditions, once the rains are established.
High nitrogen demand: split fertilization between planting and the 6- to 8-leaf stage.
The critical periods for water are flowering (heading and silking) and grain filling.
Control weeds during the first 30 to 40 days.
Monitor fall armyworm and rotate with legumes to break the pest cycle.

Frijol.descripcion: Grain legume that is a staple of the Mexican diet. It fixes atmospheric nitrogen, so it leaves the soil in better condition for a cereal in the following cycle.
Frijol.suelo: Loamy and well-drained; pH 6 to 7.5. Does not tolerate waterlogging or salinity.
cuidados: Avoid soils prone to waterlogging: the roots are sensitive to lack of oxygen.
Requires little nitrogen; prioritize phosphorus at planting.
Flowering and pod formation are the stages most sensitive to drought.
Harvest when the grain is dry to avoid rots; rain at harvest stains the grain.
Monitor whitefly, stink bug (conchuela) and diseases such as anthracnose and rust.

Trigo grano.descripcion: Winter cereal. In Mexico it is concentrated in the Fall-Winter cycle under irrigation in the northwest (Sonora, Baja California, Sinaloa) and rainfed in the Bajío and the highlands. It includes durum wheats (for pasta) and bread wheats.
Trigo grano.suelo: Loamy to clayey with good drainage; pH 6 to 7.5. Tolerates some salinity.
cuidados: Plant in the November to December window so that grain filling does not coincide with the heat.
The irrigations at tillering, heading and grain filling have the greatest influence on yield.
Fertilize with nitrogen at pre-planting and at tillering.
Monitor leaf rust and yellow rust; use resistant varieties.
Avoid lodging (the plant bending over) with adjusted nitrogen rates and irrigation.

Sorgo grano.descripcion: Heat- and drought-tolerant cereal, used mainly as livestock feed. It is common in Tamaulipas, Guanajuato and Sinaloa, and an alternative to maize where rainfall is irregular.
Sorgo grano.suelo: Adapts to many soil types; pH 5.5 to 8.5. Tolerates moderate salinity.
cuidados: Tolerates drought better than maize, but flowering remains sensitive to water shortage.
Fertilize with nitrogen at planting and at 30 days.
Monitor sugarcane aphid, a major pest in Mexico since 2013.
Control weeds in the first weeks: sorghum grows slowly at the start.
Harvest on time to reduce bird damage and rain losses.

Aguacate.descripcion: High-value perennial fruit crop; Mexico is the world's leading producer, led by Michoacán and Jalisco. The dominant variety is Hass. It enters commercial production from the third or fourth year.
Aguacate.suelo: Deep, loose and with excellent drainage; pH 5 to 7. Very sensitive to waterlogging.
cuidados: Drainage is critical: excess moisture favors avocado root rot (Phytophthora).
Regular irrigation during flowering and fruit set; water stress causes fruit drop.
Sensitive to frost; avoid low-lying areas where cold air accumulates.
Prune to keep tree height in check and let light in.
Requires phytosanitary certification for export (seed borers and branch borers).

Caña de azúcar.descripcion: Perennial industrial crop for sugar and ethanol production. It is concentrated in Veracruz, Jalisco, San Luis Potosí and Oaxaca, around the sugar mills. After planting, several ratoons are harvested.
cuidados: Needs a lot of water (more than 1,500 mm per year or supplemental irrigation).
Fertilize with nitrogen and potassium after each cut.
The harvest season (zafra) is coordinated with the sugar mill; cutting mature cane maximizes sugar content.
Renew the plantation when ratoon yields drop.
Monitor stem borer and spittlebug (mosca pinta).

Tomate rojo (jitomate).descripcion: Vegetable with the highest export value in Mexico. It is grown in open fields and increasingly in greenhouses and shade houses, especially in Sinaloa, San Luis Potosí and Michoacán.
Tomate rojo (jitomate).suelo: Loamy, rich in organic matter and well-drained; pH 5.5 to 6.8.
cuidados: Frequent and uniform irrigation (preferably drip); sudden changes in moisture crack the fruit and cause blossom-end rot.
Do not repeat solanaceous crops (chili pepper, potato, eggplant) on the same land: they share soil-borne diseases.
Stake and prune to improve ventilation and fruit quality.
Monitor whitefly and potato psyllid (they transmit viruses) and late blight.
Sensitive to frost and to low night temperatures during flowering.

Chile verde.descripcion: Includes jalapeño, serrano, poblano, bell pepper and other types. It is one of the most widespread vegetables in the country; Chihuahua, Sinaloa and Zacatecas are major producers.
Chile verde.suelo: Loamy and well-drained; pH 5.5 to 7. Sensitive to salinity and waterlogging.
cuidados: Raise seedlings in a seedbed or tray and transplant.
Light, frequent irrigations; waterlogging favors wilt (Phytophthora capsici).
Rotate with grasses; do not plant after other solanaceous crops.
Monitor pepper weevil, whitefly and viruses.
Fertilize with potassium during fruiting to improve quality.

Agave.descripcion: Long-cycle perennial plant (5 to 8 years) whose heart (piña) is used to produce tequila and mezcal. Very drought-tolerant. Jalisco concentrates most of the tequila agave, which has a designation of origin.
Agave.suelo: Stony or sandy with good drainage; pH 6 to 8.
cuidados: Very drought-tolerant; the main risk is waterlogging.
Plant healthy offshoots from selected mother plants.
Weed between rows during the first years; annual crops can be intercropped.
Monitor agave weevil and wilt.
The price is very volatile: consider contracts with the industry before planting.

Limón.descripcion: Includes Mexican (key) lime and Persian lime. Perennial warm-climate fruit crop; Michoacán, Veracruz, Colima and Oaxaca are the main producers.
Limón.suelo: Loamy to sandy and well-drained; pH 5.5 to 7.5.
cuidados: Sensitive to frost; suited to warm areas below 1,000 m a.s.l.
Regular irrigation; withholding water followed by irrigation is used to induce flowering.
Monitor HLB (huanglongbing) and its vector, the Asian citrus psyllid.
Fertilize several times a year according to expected production.
Prune for ventilation and to remove diseased branches.

Naranja.descripcion: Mexico's main citrus crop by area. Veracruz accounts for about half of production, followed by Tamaulipas and San Luis Potosí. Much of it is grown rainfed.
Naranja.suelo: Deep and with good drainage; pH 5.5 to 7.
cuidados: Under rainfed conditions, drought during flowering reduces fruit set.
Monitor HLB, fruit fly and citrus tristeza virus.
Use tristeza-tolerant rootstocks.
Lime acid soils and fertilize with nitrogen, potassium and micronutrients.
Prune to keep the canopy open.

Papa.descripcion: Tuber crop of cool temperate climates. It is grown in Sinaloa (winter), Sonora, Chihuahua, State of Mexico and other highland states.
Papa.suelo: Loose, loamy or sandy loam, deep; pH 5 to 6.5.
cuidados: Use certified virus-free seed.
Hill up (mound soil around the plant) to protect tubers from sun and pests.
Steady irrigation during tuber formation; excess water favors rots.
Monitor late blight and potato psyllid (zebra chip).
Do not repeat solanaceous crops on the same land for at least 3 years.

Alfalfa verde.descripcion: High-quality perennial forage legume for dairy cattle. It is cut several times a year for 3 to 5 years. It is concentrated in Chihuahua, Hidalgo, Guanajuato and the Comarca Lagunera.
Alfalfa verde.suelo: Deep and well-drained; pH 6.5 to 7.5. Does not tolerate acidity or waterlogging.
cuidados: Uses a lot of water: in areas with overexploited aquifers it is a contested crop.
Inoculate the seed with Rhizobium to ensure nitrogen fixation.
Cut at early flowering to balance yield and quality.
Leaves the soil rich in nitrogen for the next crop when the stand is plowed under.
Monitor aphids and armyworm.

Café cereza.descripcion: Perennial mountain shrub grown under shade in Chiapas, Veracruz, Puebla and Oaxaca, mostly by smallholders and rainfed.
Café cereza.suelo: Rich in organic matter and well-drained; pH 5 to 6.5.
cuidados: Keep shade trees to regulate temperature and conserve the soil.
Monitor coffee leaf rust and coffee berry borer; use rust-tolerant varieties.
Renew old coffee plantations to recover yield.
Pick only ripe (red) cherries to improve quality.
Grows between 600 and 1,800 m a.s.l.; lower areas are more vulnerable to heat.

Mango.descripcion: Perennial tropical fruit crop. Mexico is one of the leading exporters (Ataulfo, Tommy Atkins, Kent). It is grown in Guerrero, Sinaloa, Nayarit, Chiapas and Michoacán.
cuidados: Needs a dry season before flowering to flower well.
Rain during flowering favors anthracnose and reduces fruit set.
Monitor fruit fly (control is mandatory for export).
Prune after harvest to control tree size.
Sensitive to frost.

Cebada grano.descripcion: Cool-climate cereal used mainly by the brewing industry. It is grown rainfed in the highlands (Hidalgo, Tlaxcala, Puebla, State of Mexico) and irrigated in the Bajío.
Cebada grano.suelo: Loamy and well-drained; pH 6 to 8. Tolerates moderate salinity.
cuidados: Short cycle: useful where the rainy season is brief.
High nitrogen rates raise protein and lower malting quality.
Plant certified malting varieties if selling to the industry.
Monitor rust and aphids.
Harvest at the right grain moisture to avoid losing quality.

Garbanzo grano.descripcion: Winter legume, very drought-tolerant; it usually makes use of residual soil moisture. Sonora and Sinaloa produce white chickpea for export.
Garbanzo grano.suelo: Loamy to clayey with good drainage; pH 6 to 8.
cuidados: Tolerates drought well; excess water favors chickpea wilt (Fusarium).
Plant in Fall-Winter; a good rotation after summer maize or sorghum.
Fixes nitrogen: requires little nitrogen fertilization.
Use treated seed and varieties tolerant to root diseases.
Monitor pod borer (Helicoverpa).

Avena forrajera en verde.descripcion: Cool-climate forage cereal that is cut green or ensiled for livestock. It is grown rainfed in the highlands and irrigated in Fall-Winter.
Avena forrajera en verde.suelo: Adapts to poor and somewhat acid soils; pH 5 to 7.
cuidados: Tolerates cold and light frosts better than other cereals.
Cut at the milk-dough grain stage for good forage quality.
Can be intercropped with vetch or pea to improve protein.
Fertilize with nitrogen at planting.
Useful in rotation to cover the soil in winter.

Fresa.descripcion: High-value intensive crop, almost always with drip irrigation and plastic mulch. Michoacán (Zamora) and Baja California concentrate production, much of it for export.
Fresa.suelo: Sandy to loamy, loose and well-drained; pH 5.5 to 6.8.
cuidados: Use certified nursery plants.
Drip irrigation with fertigation; it is sensitive to salinity.
Mulch with plastic to control weeds and keep the fruit clean.
Monitor botrytis (gray mold), spider mite and thrips.
Harvest daily or every other day: requires a lot of labor.

Soya.descripcion: Oilseed legume. In Mexico it is planted in Tamaulipas, Campeche, San Luis Potosí and Chiapas, mostly rainfed in summer.
cuidados: Inoculate the seed with Bradyrhizobium if the field has not had soybean before.
Choose the variety according to latitude: flowering depends on day length.
Flowering and pod filling are the stages most sensitive to drought.
Monitor whitefly, stink bugs and Asian soybean rust.
Good rotation with maize or sorghum: it supplies nitrogen to the following cereal.

Cebolla.descripcion: Bulb vegetable planted year-round in different regions. Chihuahua, Zacatecas, Tamaulipas and Baja California are major producers.
Cebolla.suelo: Loamy, loose and well-drained; pH 6 to 7.
cuidados: Choose the variety according to the local day length (short-, intermediate- or long-day).
Shallow roots: light, frequent irrigations; stop before harvest.
Control weeds carefully: its thin foliage makes it a poor competitor.
Monitor thrips and downy mildew.
Cure (dry) the bulbs after harvest for storage.

Maíz forrajero en verde.descripcion: Maize harvested whole and green for silage to feed dairy cattle. It is concentrated in the Comarca Lagunera, Jalisco, Chihuahua and Aguascalientes.
Maíz forrajero en verde.suelo: Loamy, deep and well-drained; pH 5.5 to 7.5.
cuidados: Cut when the grain is at 1/3 to 1/2 milk line for good silage.
High water and nitrogen demand, like grain maize.
Use forage hybrids with high dry matter production.
Chop fine and pack the silo well to avoid losses.
Rotate with oats or legumes in Fall-Winter.
